name: Juuku Gorge
near: Saruu (a village on the Balykchy — Karakol highway, 42–45 km west of Karakol) — the turnoff into the gorge; the gorge entrance is about 10–12 km south of the highway.
elev: The gorge entrance at the red cliffs is ~1900–2100 m (estimate: Saruu on the shore is ~1650 m, plus a climb of 10–12 km up the valley); the middle part of the valley by the hot springs is ~2600 m (jetioguz.travel); the upper reaches — the Arabel plateau above 3700 m, the Juuku Pass 3700 m (Nomad's Land). The sources give no exact elevation for the catalogue point.
short: Juuku is the longest gorge of the Terskey Ala-Too (the river is 55 km) on the south shore of Issyk-Kul: red cliff “gates” at the bottom, spruce forests and lakes higher up, with access to the Arabel plateau and the historic route to Kashgar.
desc: Juuku Gorge begins at the village of Saruu and stretches more than 50 km into the Terskey Ala-Too, up to the Juuku Pass (3700 m) and the Arabel plateau. The lower part is known for red sandstone cliffs forming “gates”, the middle for dense spruce forests and the side gorge of Juukuchak with hot springs (the Jiluu-Suu resort), the upper for high-mountain lakes (Kashka-Suu, Chokaly-Kol and others) and glaciers. The valley has petroglyphs, Saka burial mounds of the 7th–1st centuries BC and stone statues; a caravan route to China ran over the Juuku Pass, used by Xuanzang and Semenov-Tian-Shansky. There is almost no infrastructure: no shops, cafes or guesthouses, no mobile signal, but plenty of spots for tents. The road is tolerable in the lower part and deteriorates quickly higher up — you need an SUV.
guide: Turn off the highway at Saruu and after 7 km keep right at the fork — toward Juukuchak, where, 15 km from the village, the concrete tubs of the Jiluu-Suu hot-spring resort stand; this is one of the least crowded thermal springs in the country. But the main thing is the red cliff “gates” in the lower part of Juuku: drive through them slowly, preferably in the morning when the sun colours the sandstone. Higher up come spruce trees, fords and potholes — don't go without 4WD, and after rain and during snowmelt the road turns to mud. Look for petroglyphs on the rocks and stone statues by the burial mounds — this is the ancient caravan route to Kashgar. Bring everything with you: there are no cafes or shops in the gorge, and no signal either; boil river water — livestock graze higher up.
see: The red cliff “gates” in the lower part; spruce forests; the Juukuchak hot springs (Jiluu-Suu resort); the lakes Kashka-Suu, Chokaly-Kol and Small Kashka-Suu in the upper reaches; the Juuku waterfall; petroglyphs, Saka burial mounds and stone babas; access to the Arabel plateau and the Juuku Pass (3700 m) with views of glaciers; wildlife — ibex, argali, marmots, golden eagles.
skip: You have an ordinary passenger car and aren't ready to drive through fords — beyond the first few kilometres the gorge is impassable. You need developed springs and cafes — here there are only concrete tubs and wild camping spots. You are limited to one day on the south shore — Jeti-Oguz and Barskoon are easier to reach.
diff: By car — moderate/high: ~50 km of unmaintained dirt road with fords and sharp rocks; you need an SUV with good clearance and an experienced driver. Hikes and horse trips to the lakes and the Juuku Pass (3700 m) are multi-day and high-altitude (TUK treks “Jukuchak and Juku”). A walk near the red cliffs is easy.
when: July — September (TripAdvisor: optimal; the road is passable from about April, but during snowmelt there is mud and dangerous fords). After rain the road and trails wash out. In winter the upper reaches are closed by snow.
hours: An open area, round the clock. There is a barrier at the entrance; the eco tax collection has reportedly been suspended (status unclear). The Jiluu-Suu resort operates in summer.
daytime: Morning: the red cliffs are lit up, the fords are shallower (the river rises toward the evening from glacier melt); leave Karakol early to get back before dark.
how: The Balykchy — Karakol highway to the village of Saruu (42–45 km from Karakol, ~205 km from Cholpon-Ata), turn south; after 7 km the gorge forks: the right branch — Juukuchak to the hot springs (~15 km from the village), the left — the main Juuku to the red cliffs, forest and lakes. There is no public transport in the gorge — marshrutkas (minibuses) Karakol — Balykchy along the south shore drop you in Saruu, then take a taxi/hitch a ride.
needcar: Yes, an SUV: from Saruu it is 10–12 km to the cliffs, 15 km to the springs, and fords beyond. It is far on foot from the highway; horses are available from local shepherds/CBT by arrangement.
self: Yes, in a prepared SUV with a reserve of fuel and food; no permits are needed (the border zone begins further south, in the Arabel/Kumtor area — check if you plan to go up to the plateau). There is no signal — tell someone your route.
roadtype: Paved up to Saruu; then a packed gravel road of acceptable quality in the lower part (Kolesa.kz, Too.kg), higher up — a dirt road with fords, sharp rocks and potholes, “4x4 only” (TripAdvisor 2024–2026); in snowmelt and after rain — mud.
traveltime: Karakol — Saruu ~45 km, about 1 h; Saruu — red cliffs/entrance 10–12 km, 20–30 min; Saruu — Juukuchak springs 15 km, 30–40 min; further up the gorge the speed is 10–20 km/h. Allow a full day for the gorge with the springs; 2–4 days for the lakes and the pass.
stay: There are no guesthouses, shops or cafes in the gorge (Too.kg); at the Juukuchak springs there are simple cabins of the Jiluu-Suu resort at ~300 som/day (Kolesa.kz, year not specified); lots of tent spots; guesthouses in Saruu and Kyzyl-Suu; shepherds' yurts in summer by arrangement (CBT).
net: There is no signal in the gorge (Too.kg; TripAdvisor). Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage ends at Saruu/the highway.
entry: There is a barrier at the entrance; according to TripAdvisor reviews (2024–2026) the eco tax collection is suspended/not charged — the exact amount is not published. Bathing in the Jiluu-Suu hot spring — 50 som/hour (Kolesa.kz, date not specified). The current 2026 rate is not confirmed.
transfer: No carrier offers with 2025–2026 prices were found; as a guideline, rent a 4x4 with a driver from Karakol for the day (ask Destination Karakol/Visit Karakol). TUK/Nomad's Land tours — on request.
bring: A full tank and spare fuel, a shovel/tow rope for fords, food and water for the whole day (boil river water), warm clothes (2000–3700 m), a rain jacket, a swimsuit for the springs, offline maps and GPS, a first-aid kit; in the upper reaches — a tent and sleeping bag.
warn: River fords are dangerous during snowmelt and after rain; the road has sharp rocks — a risk of a flat tyre, a spare is a must. There is no signal — help is far away. Livestock and shepherd dogs graze higher up the gorge. The upper reaches (Arabel, Kumtor) adjoin restricted zones — check with the Border Service whether permits are needed before going up to the plateau. Don't drink river water without boiling it.
food: Kumis and homemade ayran from shepherds at the jailoo (summer pasture) in summer; in Saruu and Kyzyl-Suu — simple cafes with lagman and shashlik, Issyk-Kul fish on the highway. There is no food in the gorge — bring your own.
reviews: Google Maps (“Juuku Gorge”): 4.9/5, 9 ratings as of 03.10.2026. TripAdvisor “Juuku Gorge” (Karakol): 4.5/5, 15 reviews, no. 14 of 40 (07.10.2026). Pros: the red cliff “gates”, few people, wild nature, the springs; cons: a hard road, fords, a 4x4 is needed, no infrastructure.
p.sum: Juuku is a wild gorge with no infrastructure: turn off the southern highway at Saruu (≈45 km from Karakol), then 10–12 km of dirt road to the red cliff “gates”, and after ≈7 km the right branch goes to Juukuchak and its hot tubs (100 som). Higher up are fords and rocks, so you need a 4×4 with a local driver (from Karakol ≈5000 som a day, 2024, or 9500–13,200 som per SUV via MYWAY). Bring food, water, fuel and cash with you: the gorge has no shops, guesthouses or signal. Stay in a tent by the river or in guesthouses in Kyzyl-Suu (Homestay Ak-Jol, $19 with breakfast). The multi-day trek upward (Juuku lake, the 3640–3700 m pass, Arabel) takes 3–4 days.

p.season: April–May: mud, high water at the fords. June–July: greenery, but the fords are at their highest (the water is higher toward evening). August–September: the best time — dry, lower water. October: cold, down to −10 °C at night in the upper reaches, a 34 °C soak is pleasant. November–March: the upper reaches are under snow. Ticks in the spruce forests in May–June (for the region). No crowds.
p.budget.economy: ≈1500–2500 som/person a day: marshrutka (minibus) Karakol — Saruu 70–100, on foot, a tent for free, your own food 500–800, the spring 100.
p.budget.comfort: ≈4000–8000 som/person: SUV with a driver 5000–13,200 per car (split it), a guesthouse in Kyzyl-Suu $19, Sputnik8 tour $417 per group.
p.permits: Not needed for the gorge and the springs. At the barrier there is an eco fee, reportedly suspended per 2024–2026 reviews. When going up to the Arabel plateau — a document-check checkpoint on the Kumtor road (passport, vehicle documents), a border permit is not required per 2024 data; the Kumtor mine zone is closed.
p.access: For children — the lower part (cliffs, springs) by car; for older people — only with a driver in a 4×4 (bumpy). With a stroller — no. With a dog — yes, but beware of livestock and shepherd dogs.
